text.p: Australia's biggest building materials supplier Boral Ltd was being recommended as a "buy" as signs emerged that the national residential construction cycle was in recovery mode, Morgan Stockbroking said.
"Boral's purpose is to be a world leader in the building and construction materials industry as well as a major force in energy," Morgan analysts said in a report.

In building products, net price increases remained the challenge for the Sydney-based with benefits coming from tighter price controls and expected price increases across all products, the Morgan report said.
Brick prices were showing early positive signs while an earlier seven percent plasterboard price increase was implemented last month, the analysts said.
Concrete prices were also showing signs of increasing in South Australia and Queensland and were bottoming in Victoria.
Morgan said, however,a softening United States residential market and the sale of Briar Gypsum would see Boral's second half earnings down about 23 percent.
Morgan forecast an annual net profit for the year ended June 30 of A$174 million compared with $171 million in 1995/96.
Boral management had spent a considerable amount of time restructing the group's asset base, Morgan analysts said.
About A$2.9 bilion in capital expenditure would have been spent over the four years to June, 1997, offset partly by disposals amounting to $1 billion.
Restructuring and writedown charges accounted for $373 million over the last three years, Morgan said.
At the time of writing the report, Boral shares stood at $3.78.
